candidate.title: ddRADseq
candidate.scope: The assigned ddRADseq middle row, from genomic DNA to an amplified DNA sequencing library. Its five captioned transformations are restriction digestion, barcoded adapter addition, second restriction digestion, P2 addition and amplification. The card identifies a single source row; the separately labeled upper RAD / PE RAD-Seq and lower 2b-RAD workflows are neighboring context, with no arrows connecting them to ddRADseq. The broad DNA Rearrangements and Markers heading does not group them as targets of this card. The partial bisulfite panel at far right is also outside scope. Restriction-site marks and the yellow genomic highlight annotate the input rather than forming operations. The graph preserves the poster order and preparation histories; c_dd_order and c_dd_selection separately explain the Peterson full-text interpretation. Sequencing and analysis are not depicted.

states.label: Amplified ddRADseq DNA library
features: Right endpoint is labeled DNA; insert sequence reports a reduced genomic representation.

The genomic DNA inserts are the biological sequence carrier for locus identification and polymorphism discovery/genotyping; linked barcoded adapters provide sample association. In Peterson, an inline adapter barcode can be combined with a PCR-introduced index read separately during sequencing.

For the cited Peterson implementation, represented fragments have one end generated by each restriction enzyme and lie within a selected size window; this is primary-paper interpretation, not an extra size-selection operation drawn on the poster.
Final DNA icons omit the adapter colors without depicting adapter removal.
Restriction-site polymorphisms can change locus recovery across samples; missing tags do not alone establish a biological deletion, and represented loci do not guarantee whole-genome coverage.

method_scopes.rationale: All five listed operations belong to the assigned middle row labeled ddRADseq. The card has one target row; the matching catalogue page heading and figure caption corroborate that assignment. The neighboring RAD / PE RAD-Seq and 2b-RAD rows are separate workflows, not alternatives within this row, so their graph records and implementation questions are outside this extraction. ddRAD is a supported alias, not an additional method. The graph resolves applicability at poster-depiction scope, retaining the first-digest/barcoding input history of the second digest and its downstream operations. Peterson supports the intended double-digest and size-selection architecture but differs in reaction order; c_dd_order and c_dd_selection give that primary interpretation without reassigning the drawn local instances to an incompatible preparation history.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports this candidate at its declared poster-row scope. Every captioned ddRADseq transformation is represented by a separate local operation, the six states and ten material routes agree, and there is no drawn split, pooling, compartment transfer or data integration to recover. The target is the middle ddRADseq row, not the neighboring RAD / PE RAD-Seq, 2b-RAD or partial bisulfite panels. The diagram and matching catalogue use a sequential digestion/adapter order that differs from Peterson; the candidate preserves that drawn history and explicitly confines the simultaneous-digest and size-window interpretation to the cited implementation. The genomic DNA carrier, adapter association, endpoint simplification and restriction-site sampling limitation are supported. All supplied paper leads and the literal reference are assessed without treating abstracts or metadata as full protocol verification. No consequential unsupported claim, omitted in-scope transformation or unresolved architecture-changing question remains.

evidence.locator: Abstract, RESULTS, named MiddRAD adaptation.
evidence.quote: We refer to this simplified protocol as MiddRAD and we demonstrated the utility and flexibility of our approach by resolving phylogenetic relationships of two genera of woody bamboos (Dendrocalamus and Phyllostachys).

checks.rationale: The abstract describes a snail RAD-marker association application, not a particular preparation sequence. The unassigned background assessment and lack of library-chemistry claims are supported.

evidence.locator: Abstract, METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS, RADres association.
evidence.quote: We first identify a genomic region, RADres, showing the highest differentiation between susceptible and resistant inbred lines among 1611 informative restriction-site associated DNA (RAD) markers, and show that it significantly influences resistance in an independent set of 439 outbred snails.
